PATCH for Partial Updates

Every field optional, but not zero fields — and why that's PATCH's job, not PUT's.

REST gives updates two different verbs (Lesson 1's REST topic), and they mean different things: PUT replaces a resource entirely — every field, in one request, including ones that aren't changing — while PATCH changes only the fields it's given. A ticket update in this API is almost always "mark this resolved" or "reassign this agent," not "resend the whole ticket back with one field different," so PATCH is the one this project implements.

// Figure 3.8: every field optional, but at least one required (src/validators/ticket.validators.js, excerpt)
export const updateTicketSchema = z
  .object({
    subject: z.string().trim().min(1).max(200).optional(),
    description: z.string().trim().min(1).optional(),
    status: statusEnum.optional(),
    assignedAgentId: z.coerce.number().int().positive().nullable().optional(),
  })
  .refine((data) => Object.keys(data).length > 0, {
    message: 'at least one field must be provided',
  });

Every field carries .optional() — that's what makes this a partial update schema rather than createTicketSchema's all-required version (previous topic). But an empty {} body technically satisfies "every field is optional" too, and a PATCH that changes nothing is a request that did nothing useful. .refine(...) is Zod's escape hatch for a rule that isn't about one field's shape but the object as a whole: a function that returns true (valid) or false (invalid, using the given message) run after the individual field checks already passed. Here, it just checks that parsing actually produced at least one key.
